text: {"distance_m": 3, "reasoning_short": "Spot detection, not acuity, is the limit, and for spots this small threshold contrast scales roughly with 1/(angle²) (Ricco's law). From Blackwell-type data recalled from memory (not exact), a 1′ disc needs roughly 50% contrast at photopic levels. A 15% spot therefore needs about 1′ × √(0.5/0.15) ≈ 1.8–2′, a little more under dimmer indoor light. A 2 mm spot subtends 2′ (5.8e-4 rad) at about 3.4 m, so reliable detection is roughly 3 m. Treat this as an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a precise limit."}
